hook.text: Every car—even an EV—has a small 12-volt battery under the hood. It runs nearly everything you touch.

buildup.text: Lights, wipers, radio, power windows, and the computer that starts your engine all use 12 volts.

discovery.text: In gas cars, the alternator charges this battery while driving, using a belt connected to the engine.

twist.text: In EVs, a DC-DC converter steps down the high-voltage battery to keep the 12-volt system alive.

climax.text: If the 12-volt battery dies, even a fully charged EV won't start—it can't wake up its own computers.

punchline.text: The smallest battery in the car is also the most critical.

quiz.question: What happens if an EV's 12-volt battery dies?
options: Nothing, the main battery takes over

details.summary: Every car has a 12-volt electrical system powered by a lead-acid battery and alternator that supplies energy to start the engine and operate lights, sensors, and electronic accessories.
details.whyItMatters: Even EVs with massive high-voltage batteries still rely on a 12-volt system for essential functions. A dead 12-volt battery can leave any car stranded regardless of other power sources.
takeaways: The 12-volt battery starts the engine and powers accessories
An alternator recharges the battery while the engine runs
Even EVs use a small 12-volt battery for controls and electronics

faq.question: Why do EVs still need a 12-volt battery?
faq.answer: The 12-volt system powers low-voltage electronics like door locks, lights, and the computer that controls the high-voltage battery. It acts as a safety-isolated layer between you and dangerous voltages.

faq.question: How long does a typical car battery last?
faq.answer: Most lead-acid car batteries last 3 to 5 years depending on climate and usage. Extreme heat degrades them faster. Many auto parts stores offer free battery testing to check remaining capacity.
